From a single RGB-D image, DLONet densely traces multiple deformable linear objects (cables) and recovers a globally consistent over/under occlusion ordering for wire-harness assembly. A three-stage pipeline (TraceNet → RelationNet → GraphNet) propagates predictions together with their confidences, so local pairwise relations are reconciled into a cycle-free global layer order.

**Highlights**

- Tracing success rate 0.89 vs. 0.67 for HANDLOOM; 94.3% crossing-relation accuracy; 88.6% topologically-correct rate in multi-cable scenes.
- Frontier VLMs (GPT-5.2, Claude Opus 4.6, Qwen2.5-VL-72B) are near chance on multi-cable ordering zero-shot.
- Deployed on a Kinova Gen3 with a RealSense D435i: 90% success on real cable extraction.

**My contributions**

- Designed and trained the three network stages: TraceNet (dense centerline/event/keypoint heatmaps + embedding field, curvature-regularized decoder), RelationNet (event validity, over/under, signed depth with heteroscedastic uncertainty), and GraphNet (message passing to suppress ordering cycles; continuous Layer Field).
- Ran all baseline and VLM evaluations (HANDLOOM reproduction; zero-shot GPT-5.2 / Claude Opus 4.6 / Qwen2.5-VL-72B) and the ablation study.
- Built the Kinova Gen3 + RealSense D435i cable-extraction demo (90% success).
- Co-developed the ~35k-scene synthetic data pipeline (procedural cables, mass–spring relaxation, Blender rendering, auto-annotation) and the 100-scene real MDLO benchmark.
- Led writing and rebuttal across the ECCV 2026 and RA-L submissions; owned multi-GPU training infrastructure on Georgia Tech PACE.

<small>*Equal contribution. Full author list will appear with the arXiv version.</small>
